# R0 Digest — Author's Preface (lines 172–194)
**Source:** Tsumura, *The First Book of Samuel* (NICOT, 2006)
**Reader:** main-thread
**Coverage:** lines 172–194 read in full (Author's Preface only; Abbreviation List excluded)

## Claims

### C-R0-01 | Dialogue partners McCarter and R. P. Gordon
- **Claim (attributed Tsumura):** Primary learned-from commentaries are P. K. McCarter and R. P. Gordon; Tsumura “often disagree[s] with them.”
- **Quote:** “Among many, I have especially learned from the commentaries of P. K. McCarter and R. P. Gordon, though I often disagree with them.”
- **Locus:** Preface p. xi / raw ~L176
- **Targets:** [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R0-02 | Formation under C. H. Gordon (Ugaritic / Canaanite religion)
- **Claim:** Training in Semitic philology, especially Ugaritic, and Canaanite religion under the late C. H. Gordon prepared Tsumura for new suggestions on 1 Samuel.
- **Quote:** “training in Semitic philology, especially in Ugaritic, as well as in Canaanite religion by the late Prof. C. H. Gordon has prepared me to make some new suggestions”
- **Locus:** Preface p. xi / raw ~L178
- **Targets:** [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R0-03 | Acknowledgments (Millard, Ishida, Hubbard)
- **Claim:** A. Millard (Liverpool) commented on drafts; T. Ishida (former Tsukuba colleague) especially on introductory section; series editor R. L. Hubbard improved style and content. Tsumura fully responsible for content.
- **Quote:** “Prof. A. Millard of Liverpool University read many parts of the draft… Prof. T. Ishida… especially on the introductory section. The series editor Prof. R. L. Hubbard…”
- **Locus:** Preface p. xi / raw ~L178
- **Targets:** [[david-tsumura]], source page

### C-R0-04 | MT-first method without easy LXX emendation
- **Claim:** Tsumura sticks to MT as much as possible without easy emendation from LXX and other versions — not because MT is perfect, but to test whether present knowledge of Hebrew grammar and style (including discourse grammar / supra-sentential analysis and styles discussed) can make good sense of MT itself.
- **Quote:** “I have stuck to the MT as much as possible, without easy recourse to emendation on the basis of the LXX and other ancient versions, not because the MT is perfect, but because it is time again to read the MT straightforwardly and determine whether, with the present knowledge of Hebrew grammar and style, we can make good sense out of the MT itself — the grammar includes, of course, discourse grammar, that is, supra-sentential grammatical analysis”
- **Locus:** Preface p. xi / raw ~L180
- **Targets:** [[david-tsumura]], [[1-samuel]] (Hermeneutical Frameworks / Text-Critical)

### C-R0-05 | Comparatively literal translation practice
- **Claim:** Translation is comparatively literal: *waw* as “and” where possible; original word order reflected where possible; some idioms/formulae non-literal (e.g. dropping “and said” from “answered and said”).
- **Quote:** “This is a comparatively literal translation. For instance, waw is translated as “and” where possible… Also, where possible, the original word order is reflected”
- **Locus:** Preface pp. xi–xii / raw ~L182
- **Targets:** [[david-tsumura]], source page

### C-R0-06 | Institutional and personal setting
- **Claim:** Japan Bible Seminary faculty/students (Pres. S. Funaki; Profs. K. Uchida, T. Matsumoto) and Hamadayama Church members supported the project; dedicated to wife Susan and sons Michio and Makoto; Greek 2 Cor 12:9 as dedication verse.
- **Quote:** “To her and my sons I dedicate this book with love.” + 2 Cor 12:9 Greek
- **Locus:** Preface p. xii / raw ~L186–189
- **Targets:** [[david-tsumura]]

## Coverage note
Preface only; no commentary body in this range.
